Stable-graph counting: each of the n labelled legs lies on one vertex and each edge contributes one half-edge to each end, so sum_v n_v = n+2|E|. Arithmetic genus gives sum_v g_v = g-b_1 with b_1=|E|-|V|+1. Substituting yields sum_v (2g_v-2+n_v)=2g-2+n. Stack-level, Q-irrelevant combinatorics; no coarse-space identification.

S:={stable (g',n'): g'<=5 and a(g',n'):=2g'-2+n'<=16} contains (5,8) since a(5,8)=16. One-edge vertices have g_v<=g and, by CLM-0145-1 plus stability a_v>=1, each a_v<=a(g,n)<=16, so S is closed under one-edge vertex types. Dimension drop is d-1 for both the loop (d(g-1,n+2)=d-1) and a separating edge (d1+d2=d-1). RED-0001 members with g>=6 are excluded by g'<=5. The remaining list members (5,8) and (3,12) both have a=16; a vertex with a_v=16 is necessarily the unique vertex, hence the empty graph when g_v=5 and the two-loop graph (b_1=2, n_v=8+4=12) when g_v=3. No other RED-0001 pair lies in S.

SRC-0002 Eq. (6.1)/THM-0003 is the right-exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures H_k(hat{partial})->H_k(Mbar)->W_{-k}H^{BM}_k(M)->0, scoped to all stable (g,n) and all k. Duality on finite-dimensional Q-MHS reverses arrows and converts right-exactness into left-exactness. For proper DM stacks, H_k(-;Q) is dual to H^k(-;Q), so at k=16 one obtains 0->K(g,n)->H^{16}(Mbar_{g,n};Q)->H^{16}(hat{partial}Mbar_{g,n};Q) with no Gysin shift and no extra Tate twist. hat{partial} is the disjoint union over one-edge graphs of [Mbar_Gamma/Aut(Gamma)] by Knudsen clutching (packet convention); with Q-coefficients H^{16}([Mbar_Gamma/Aut];Q)=H^{16}(Mbar_Gamma;Q)^{Aut}. ATT-0141 (C58-BOUNDARY-001/002, REV-0190/REV-0192) specialises this at (5,8).

A one-edge graph has Aut acting on a one-element edge set, so det E_Gamma is at worst a sign character chi. For W a finite direct sum of Q(-8), any subspace of (W tensor chi), in particular the invariants (W tensor chi)^A, remains of Hodge type (8,8). This is only an upper bound of Tate type; it does not identify ranks. At (5,8), ATT-0141/REV-0192 give Aut trivial on every separating graph (g1+g2=5 odd, legs labelled) and Aut=S_2 only on [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2]. Homology of a quotient is coinvariants, cohomology is invariants; dual of coinvariants is invariants, so the convention is consistent across (*).

Excluding (3,12) and (5,8), THM-0005/SRC-0002 Table 1 and Proposition 4.5 apply on the OPEN stack at every pure-weight degree: genus 0 unrestricted, g=3 with n<=11=c(3), g=4 with n<=10<=11=c(4), g=5 with n<=7=c(5). THM-0006 (SRC-0002: 'When g=1, all even cohomology is tautological [26]', scoped even/all n) and THM-0007 (SRC-0002 Corollary 2.7: H^{2k}(Mbar_{2,n})=RH^{2k} for k<=10, all n) apply at degree 16, i.e. k=8<=10. Tautological classes are algebraic of type (p,p); THM-0001 gives purity of weight 16, so the groups are finite direct sums of Q(-8) (empty when 16>2d). This shortcuts genus 1 and 2 entirely, so the published c(1)=c(2)=10 range is never invoked, even though S contains (1,n) up to n=16 and (2,n) up to n=14.

Kunneth for Q-MHS on a product of two proper stacks: summands with i+j=16 and i,j both odd are the pairs (1,15),(3,13),(5,11),(7,9) and swaps, so min(i,j) is in {1,3,5,7}. SRC-0001 Section 2.4 (notation: Mg,n is the smooth proper stack of stable curves) records H^k(Mbar_{g,n})=0 for odd k<11, all g,n, citing BFP24; SRC-0003 introduction independently records vanishing for odd k<=9, all g,n. The argument only needs k<=7, well inside both statements. In particular H^{11} (which may carry S_{12}) never pairs with a nonzero odd partner in total degree 16. No point count or Serre characteristic is used.

Induction on d=3g-3+n is well-founded. Base d<=7: 16>2d so H^{16}=0. For g in {1,2} apply CLM-0145-7. Otherwise CLM-0145-5/6 type K; CLM-0145-2 puts every one-edge factor in S at dimension d-1; Step 6 types H^{16}(Mbar_Gamma) by IH on the (16,0) and (0,16) Kunneth slots, THM-0002 (SRC-0002 Theorem 1.5(3): H^k(Mbar) congruent to Q(-k/2) for even k<=14, all g,n) on even slots with 2<=i,j<=14, and CLM-0145-8 on odd-odd slots; CLM-0145-4 preserves Tate type under Aut/det. Sequence (*) realises H^{16}(Mbar) as an extension of a subobject of a Q(-8) sum by a Q(-8) sum. THM-0001: Mbar and hat{partial} (disjoint union of smooth proper stack quotients) have H^{16} pure of weight 16. FND-0033: polarizable pure Q-HS of a fixed weight are semisimple, so the subobject is Q(-8)^{oplus} and the extension splits as an actual Hodge-structure isomorphism, not merely a semisimplification.

Specialise CLM-0145-9 at (5,8) in S with d=20. Kernel of (*) is K(5,8), typed Q(-8)^{oplus} by ATT-0142. The target is H^{16} of the ATT-0141 components [Mbar_{4,10}/S_2] and separating products with g1+g2=5, n1+n2=10, all in S at dimension 19 and covered by the Proposition, THM-0002, and odd vanishing; maximal types (4,10),(5,7),(3,9) are handled by THM-0005 (10<=c(4), 7=c(5), 9<=c(3)) plus their own boundary induction, which is where (3,12) enters as the non-separating divisor of Mbar_{4,10} and is discharged by CLM-0145-6. Poincare on the smooth proper 20-fold: H^{16}=Q(-8)^{oplus b} iff H_{16}=Q(8)^{oplus b} iff H^{24} congruent to Hom(H^{16},Q(-20))=Q(-12)^{oplus b}. Rank b>=0 is admitted; no tautological-generation or algebraic-cycle upgrade of H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8}) is claimed.

finding_candidates.statement: For a stable graph of type (g,n), sum over vertices of a(g_v,n_v):=2g_v-2+n_v equals a(g,n). Consequently the set S of stable pairs with g'<=5 and a(g',n')<=16 is closed under passing to vertex types of one-edge graphs, each such factor has dimension one less, and S meets the RED-0001 list exactly in (5,8) (the empty graph) and (3,12) (the unique vertex of a two-loop graph, equivalently the non-separating divisor of Mbar_{4,10}). Compact H^{16} on S can therefore be assembled from THM-0003, published CKgP on every other open corner, the verified (5,8) open residual, and a single FND-0195 evaluation at (3,12); the informal slogan that the boundary of Mbar_{5,8} lies outside RED-0001 is not used and is false beyond codimension one.

finding_candidates.statement: In the Kunneth decomposition of H^{16}(Mbar_{g1,n1} x Mbar_{g2,n2};Q), every summand with both degrees odd has min(i,j) in {1,3,5,7}. Vanishing of H^k(Mbar_{g,n};Q) for odd k<=7, all g,n (BFP24, recorded in SRC-0001 Section 2.4 and SRC-0003), therefore kills every odd-odd term. In particular a copy of S_{12} in H^{11} cannot contribute to a product in total degree 16, because its complementary factor would have to be H^5=0. No point count, Serre characteristic, or vanishing in degrees 9,11,13,15 is required for this parity separation.

strongest_attack: The strongest attack is that the induction is not a one-edge argument on Mbar_{5,8} at all: H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8}) requires H^{16}(Mbar_{4,10}), whose non-separating divisor is Mbar_{3,12}, and (3,12) is itself a RED-0001 residual pair. Typing K(3,12) is then a zero-slack FND-0195 instance (n-1=11=c(3), k=vcd=20=2d-16), with all Hodge type carried by the single CKgP evaluation W_{18}H^{18}(M_{3,11};Q)=Q(-9)^a on the OPEN stack; every other peel vanishing has slack of one (20>19, 8>7). This is the same single point of failure as ATT-0142 at (5,8) and FND-0195 at (6,6), and it is exactly the depth-two phenomenon that makes the informal plan step 'the boundary of Mbar_{5,8} lies outside RED-0001' false beyond codimension one. The attack was pressed and fails. FND-0195 is corroborated for g>=2, n>=1, k=vcd, with the inclusive published table that names c(3)=11; neither listed exclusion (degree vcd-1, unpublished c(8)) is engaged; the internals were re-derived at (3,12) rather than imported from the (6,6) or (5,8) arithmetic; THM-0005/Prop 4.5 types every W_k H^k of open M_{3,11} with no degree restriction, so the source degree 18=vcd(M_{3,11})-1 is irrelevant to CKgP. The argument never uses 'outside RED-0001' as a Tate hypothesis: (3,12) is met head-on, and every other K on S is typed by THM-0005 inside n<=c(g) or by ATT-0142. Secondary attacks, all of which failed. (1) Dualizing THM-0003 might smuggle a Gysin shift or det-E twist: Eq. (6.1) is ordinary homology of hat{partial}, so dualisation is restriction H^{16}(Mbar)->H^{16}(hat{partial}) with no twist; det-E is a graph-complex/weight-spectral-sequence decoration, and even if imposed it is at worst a sign character on a one-edge graph whose invariants cannot enlarge Hodge type. (2) Odd-odd Kunneth could carry S_{12} from H^{11} tensor H^5: min(i,j)<=7, and BFP24 vanishing on compact Mbar (SRC-0001 Section 2.4, SRC-0003; notation Mg,n = stable-curve stack) kills the smaller factor. (3) Genus 1 and 2 in S overflow c(1)=c(2)=10: they are not routed through K at all, but through THM-0006 (all even degrees, all n) and THM-0007 at k=8<=10. (4) Semisimplification versus isomorphism: all three terms of (*) are polarizable pure of weight 16, so FND-0033 makes the extension an honest split as Q(-8) sums. (5) Stack versus coarse and Q versus Z: all identifications are stack-level with Q-coefficients; H^*([X/G];Q)=H^*(X)^G, and invariants equal coinvariants rationally. (6) Pure Tate upgraded to algebraic or tautological generation of H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8}): the theorem asserts only Tate type; tautological generation is used only as a stronger input from THM-0006/0007/0002 to deduce type (8,8). (7) Predicted motives used as theorems: none; algebraicity enters only through CKgP or tautological spanning. (8) Omitted stable pairs: S is closed under one-edge vertex types and contains every separating type with g1+g2=g and n1+n2=n+2 subject to stability; pairs with g>=6 are excluded by the genus bound. (9) Forbidden at-vcd vanishing and CGP top-weight: not used. (10) Punctured-curve mixed R^1 (FND-0020/FND-0037): the only Leray input is the closed universal curve inside FND-0195. Confirming this lemma does not verify the campaign boundary-image theorem, H^{16}(Mbar_{6,6}), or CONJ-0001.
theorem_statement: Using a verified C58-OPEN residual and a verified C58-BOUNDARY accounting, apply the boundary right-exact sequence of THM-0003 to conclude that H^{16}(Mbar_{5,8};Q) is a finite direct sum of Q(-8). A disproof must exhibit a surviving non-Tate summand in this compact group. This theorem does not conclude the campaign boundary-image theorem.
